account: Today has mostly been ordinary mayoral business: a market walk, town accounts, and tea with the neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage. The tea invitation lacked a precise address, so the secretary went to confirm it. I did not clearly hear her attempts to reach me and arrived at the cottage at 15:19, then returned late for my 16:30 office appointment. The neighbour was well and described enjoying the dock and chatting with neighbours. The only unusual matter is a vague rumour the neighbour heard about a bridge or port change. They had not seen anything themselves and could not confirm it. The secretary likewise reports no correspondence or confirmed proposal, so I do not know whether any change is actually contemplated, who might be behind it, or what its purpose would be. I asked her not to circulate the rumour as fact and to check for correspondence needing a decision. She has since placed two books in the appointments chest; I have seen the books there but have not yet read them. She says tomorrow includes office at eight and a grain inspection at the mill at ten, for which I requested papers. My next scheduled commitment is home at nineteen hundred.
